text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Monday:

- Citizens of Appenzell Ausserrhoden canton decided to hold a referendum on whether to get rid of the so-called Landsgemeinde, a 400-year-old democratic insitution where citizens meet to vote. Women's suffrage has made the gathering too large, and some voters prefer a secret ballot.
- Swiss Justice Minister Arnold Koller told criminologists that he will announce a package of increased legal sanctions against corruption toward the end of the year.
- The Swiss government is currently investigating the possibility of changing its refugee policy, making it more difficult for ethinc groups in large numbers to receive asylum.
- The Swiss Greens Party said it will support a public initiative to ban Swiss arms exports.

- Christoph Blocher, right-wing populist and member of parliament, said at a gathering of the pro-neutrality Auns group that the Swiss government did not counter firmly enough 'the excessive, unfounded accusations and the extortionist demands for money form New York'. He was referring to Jewish groups' calls for Switzerland to make compensation for its close commercial ties to Nazi Germany and Swiss banks' handling of dormant accounts deposited by Holocaust victims

- Jean-Pascal Delamuraz, Switzerland's economics minister, said in an interview with French-speaking Swiss radio that 'failure of the bilateral negotiations with the European Union would be a catastrophe for Switzerland'.
